title: Distributed Sliding Window Rate Limiter with Redis Race Conditions
businessContext: A public developer API allows 100 requests per minute per API key. Under distributed load test across 8 API server instances, clients are able to send 250 requests per minute because of a Read-Modify-Write race condition in the Redis rate limiting logic.
problemStatement: The current implementation fetches the count from Redis with `GET`, checks if `count < 100` in Node.js, and then issues `INCR`. Concurrently arriving requests all read `count = 99` before any of them increments, permitting burst overages. Implement an atomic sliding-window rate limiter using Redis Lua scripting or atomic multi-exec pipelines.
constraints: Must guarantee strict enforcement of 100 req/60s across distributed cluster.
Must be fully atomic: zero window race conditions.
Return remaining tokens and reset timestamp in standard headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
candidateTasks: Explain the Read-Modify-Write race condition across distributed API servers.
Implement an atomic rate limiter using Redis Lua script or sorted sets (`ZADD`, `ZREMRANGEBYSCORE`, `ZCARD`).
Explain the difference between Fixed Window Counter, Sliding Log (Sorted Set), and Sliding Window Counter.
hints: Redis executes Lua scripts atomically: no other command can run while the script executes.
Alternatively, for a fixed window, `INCR` followed by `EXPIRE` on first increment (or `SET key 1 NX EX 60`) provides atomicity.

testCases.name: Atomically evaluates rate limit with zero race conditions
testCases.explanation: Enforces strict quota under high concurrency.

alternativeApproaches: Generic Cell Rate Algorithm (GCRA) / Leaky Bucket using Redis `redis-cell` module.
Cloudflare / AWS WAF edge rate limiting.
commonMistakes: Using Fixed Window which allows 2x limit bursts at window boundaries (e.g. 100 requests at 0:59 and 100 requests at 1:01).
Forgetting to set TTL/EXPIRE on the Redis key, leaking memory indefinitely.
